question_type: natural log of the ratio of one named total (Treasury Survey of Ownership table) at two as-of dates ten years apart

opus_path.decision: Read the question's phrase 'Interest-Bearing Public Marketable Securities ... by issues' as the verbatim title of Treasury Survey of Ownership Section I Table 3; 'Total ... Outstanding' = row 'Total public marketable securities', column 'Total amount outstanding'. Treated Jan 31 as the survey (as-of) date, not the issue date, and expected a lag (Jan 31 surveys print in the April issues).

Enumerated every candidate 'marketable' total in the early-1948 issues (debt-limitation 'Total marketable issues', the maturity schedule, the Survey of Ownership) and rejected the maturity schedule (no grand total, excludes postal savings bonds) and the March issue's survey (dated Dec 31).
Found the Jan 31, 1948 and Jan 31, 1958 surveys in the April issues (1948_04:1870/1940, 1958_04:2362/2365); the March issues carry the Dec 31 surveys.
Read both full tables, confirmed '(Par values - in millions of dollars)', summed the components to the printed total, and resolved an OCR conflict in Table 1 by using that table's own grand total.
Reconciled the survey totals with the debt-limitation 'Total marketable' rows: the debt statement excludes the guaranteed FHA debentures, so it is a different scope, not a different vintage.
Checked for reprints/revisions of the Jan 31 survey totals across the corpus; single-print, no vintage conflict.
Computed ln(1948/1958) in calc.py with component asserts; recorded the debt-limitation and maturity-schedule alternatives and noted they give materially different log values.

opus_key_moves: Matched the question's distinctive phrase ('... by issues') to a table TITLE verbatim instead of to a row label that only partly matched
Enumerated the competing 'total marketable' rows and reconciled them (debt statement = survey total minus guaranteed FHA debentures), so the scope difference was explicit before choosing
Used the survey's as-of date to pick the April issue (survey lag), rejecting the March issue whose survey is dated Dec 31

adapter_context.notes: The cited lesson is correct for its own question ('fixed maturity type' from the maturity schedule) but is not about this series; it pulled the actor into the March-bulletin debt section. The debt-limitation lesson gives a ready-made definition of 'Total marketable', which made the wrong row look sanctioned. The TSO lesson that names the right family states the cadence 'Jan 31 -> the MARCH bulletin', verified only for the 1960s-70s; in 1948 and 1958 the March issue carries the Dec 31 survey and the Jan 31 survey is in April, so even retrieving it would have mis-pointed the issue unless the actor checked the printed survey date.

remedies.intervention: A table-title index/search: list every table title (with its as-of date and issue) whose title matches the question's quoted or Title-Case phrase, ranked by title overlap, filterable by as-of date. Query 'Interest-Bearing Public Marketable Securities by Issues' + 'January 31, 1948' would return 1948_04 TSO Table 3 first.
remedies.why: The none arm reached the right table only because one FTS query happened to keep 'by issues' + date + filename_glob ([17]); the prompt arm's generic FTS queries ([6],[10],[15],[20]) never surfaced it.

remedies.intervention: Mandatory candidate-table stage: before extracting, list at least two candidate tables with their exact titles and score each against the question's noun phrase; choosing a candidate whose title does not contain the question's distinctive qualifier ('by issues') requires an explicit scope reconciliation (which components differ).
remedies.why: At [27] the actor itself noticed the mismatch ('by issues' vs 'Marketable issues') but had no alternative on screen; a forced enumeration would have sent it looking for a title match.

remedies.intervention: Series-location memory keyed by (table family, era) with the verified issue lag per era and a check cell, retrieved by the question's dates: e.g. TSO Jan 31 survey -> April issue in 1948/1958, March issue in the 1960s-70s.
remedies.why: The prompt arm's text memory had a TSO entry but with a single-era cadence and was not retrieved; a retrieval keyed by date range would both surface the family and give the right lag.

remedies.intervention: Sensitivity check for log-ratios/differences of near-equal quantities: when |ratio-1| is small, require the actor to show that both endpoints have the same scope (component list sums to the chosen total) before committing.
remedies.why: The scope difference here is a small guaranteed-debenture component, invisible at the level but decisive for the log; the actor never looked at components.

right_arms_note: none: its FTS query kept the qualifier 'by issues' with the date and a per-year filename_glob ([17]), which ranked the April Survey of Ownership Table 3 into the results; the two wrong arms dropped the qualifier or searched case-sensitively and only ever saw the March issues.
text_vs_mechanism: Text alone is unlikely to fix this: the prompt arm had ~230 KB of lessons, including one that names the right table family, yet the text it did retrieve steered it to the wrong family and the right lesson carried an era-limited cadence. The failures are retrieval failures (case-sensitive substring search, BM25 ranking without title/date filters), so a title-aware, case-insensitive search tool plus a candidate-table stage is the better lever.
notes: Both wrong arms converged on the same debt-limitation row by the same partial-match rationalisation ('by issues' -> 'Marketable issues'), which suggests the actor accepts a partial lexical match when the exact one is not on screen. The error_bin '>25pct' overstates the level error: the scopes differ by a tiny guaranteed-securities component, which a log of a near-1 ratio magnifies. Harness lesson: for answers that are logs/differences of near-equal totals, scope reconciliation is the main risk.
